claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 healthy controls showed increased frequencies of plasmablasts and effector CD8 T cells in infected individuals compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients by mass cytometry
sources.quote: There was a notable increase in the frequency of plasmablast and effector CD8 T cells in all infected individuals (Fig. 1B) in both cohorts.

comparison.finding: increased frequencies of plasmablasts and effector CD8 T cells in infected individuals compared to healthy controls

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells in response to TLR stimulation compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: COVID-19 results in functional impairment of blood myeloid cells and pDCs
sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls (Fig. 2A).

comparison.finding: reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells in response to TLR stimulation in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls

claim_3.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed significant up-regulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
sources.quote: Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection (Fig. 3, top row, and fig. S6).

comparison.finding: significant up-regulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10

claim_4.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients revealed clusters of T cells and monocytes characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes such as IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15, which were not present in healthy controls.

sources.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15 (see C11-C MONO_IFN and C18-T_IFN in fig. S10).

comparison.finding: clusters of T cells and monocytes characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes such as IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15 were present in COVID-19 patients but not in healthy controls

claim_5.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed a strong induction of interferon-stimulated genes compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
sources.quote: We observed a strong induction of the ISGs in COVID-19 subjects compared with healthy donors in this dataset as well (Fig. 4G).

comparison.finding: strong induction of interferon-stimulated genes in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls

claim_6.claim: Q-PCR analysis of plasma from severe and ICU COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Severe COVID-19 infection is associated with the systemic release of bacterial products
sources.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product.

comparison.finding: severe and ICU COVID-19 patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA compared to healthy controls
